evals.prompt: We're adding a 'Delete workspace' button to the settings page. It should be a red button with a confirm dialog that says 'Are you sure?' with OK and Cancel. Spec the right interaction.
evals.expected_output: A spec that names object, scope, and consequence; treats the action as irreversible and wide-scope; replaces OK/Cancel with a typed or named confirmation; enumerates in-progress and failure states; routes the build to ui-design and final wording to ghostwriter.
assertions: Cites rule/irreversible-action-safeguard or rule/destructive-proportional for the safeguard choice
Cites rule/destructive-names-action or rule/no-confirm-ok-labels and rejects OK as the confirm label
States the scope (everything in the workspace, every member) before the user commits
Does not emit a code patch, className, or prop change
Every cited rule ID appears verbatim in references/rules.md

evals.prompt: Design the flow for reordering items in our mobile task list. Product wants drag-to-reorder like Things 3.
evals.expected_output: Drag-to-reorder accepted as the primary interaction, with a single-pointer alternative (move up/down or a Move-to menu) required, the states enumerated (sparse list, drag in progress, save failure with rollback), and the gesture physics routed to ui-animation.
assertions: Cites rule/gesture-has-control-alternative and names a concrete non-drag alternative
Lists a failure state for the reorder save
Cites rule/cover-reachable-states
Routes the gesture implementation to ui-animation, not to itself
Includes an internal brief with job, desired outcome, and consequence filled

evals.prompt: What breaks here? Our checkout collects shipping address on step 2, then asks for the billing address on step 4 with no prefill. Session times out after 10 minutes and dumps you back to the cart. Unsaved fields are lost.
evals.expected_output: A harden-mode findings list ordered P0 to P3: redundant entry (billing not prefilled from shipping), silent session expiry that discards input, lost user input, each with rule ID, user consequence, and the smallest fix and owning skill.
assertions: Cites rule/no-redundant-entry for the billing address re-entry
Cites rule/time-limit-adjustable for the session timeout and proposes a warning plus extension or draft persistence
Cites rule/preserve-user-input for the lost fields
Findings carry a P0-P3 level and a user consequence, not only a code observation

evals.prompt: Support keeps getting tickets about accidental archives, so the squad wants a confirm dialog on Archive project. Do we need it? Notes are in archive-flow.md.
evals.expected_output: A short action-mode answer: no confirmation on Archive because it is fully restorable, the existing Delete forever safeguard left as it is, and at most a pointer from the toast to where the project went.
assertions: Recommends against adding the confirmation dialog to Archive project
Gives the unlimited Restore from the Archived tab as the reason Archive needs no confirmation
Says that confirming a reversible action teaches people to click through confirmations
Does not recommend changing the Delete forever dialog
Cites rule/destructive-proportional

evals.prompt: Review this invite flow for product correctness before we build it. The spec is invite-flow.md.
evals.expected_output: Review-mode findings ordered by user impact: pasted addresses lost on any failure, a seat charge the dialog never states, a dialog stacked on a dialog, each with the consequence and the smallest decision-level fix.
assertions: Flags that a failed Submit discards the pasted email addresses
Flags that the dialog does not tell the user each invite reserves a paid seat before they commit
Flags the personal note dialog opening on top of the Invite dialog
Lists the lost-addresses finding above the stacked-dialog finding
Every finding carries a rule ID written in the rule/<name> form

evals.prompt: Choose the controls for our notification settings screen. Brief is in notification-brief.md, the UI team builds it after.
evals.expected_output: A shape-mode decision per setting: a single-choice control for frequency, a multi-select for channels, a searchable picker for time zone, the native time inputs kept, with translated label length accounted for.
assertions: Chooses a single-choice control (radio group or segmented control) for digest frequency instead of checkboxes
Chooses a multi-select control (checkboxes or switches) for channels instead of the single-select dropdown
Chooses a searchable select or combobox for time zone instead of the radio list
Keeps the native time inputs for quiet hours
Says how the digest frequency control copes with longer German or Japanese labels
